messages:
maria: seeing a spike in pod-to-pod packet loss across gpu-ns, started ~09:12 UTC after the network-policy rollout. GPU heartbeats dropping and some nodes marking NotReady. Anyone else?

owen: yep getting alerts. tcp retransmits between inference replicas up ~40%. TL;DR: east-west traffic between pods in gpu-ns is being denied intermittently.

jin: logs show a bunch of conntrack entries in TIME_WAIT then immediate drops. could be conntrack exhaustion. can you paste conntrack stats?

maria: grabbing quick outputs:```
# conntrack -S
entries: 262144
searched: 1.2M
found: 1.1M
new: 80k
deleted: 70k
insert_failed: 3k
search_restart: 15k
```
insert_failed seems high.

sam: insert_failed 3k is suspicious. what changed in policy? deploy-bot: network-policy/v1 applied gpu-namespace/deny-egress-from-sidecars (revision 2026-03-18T08:50:12Z)

ravi: that policy had a blanket egress deny + specific allow for svc selectors. If some pods use ephemeral hostNetwork or non-matching labels, packets may be hitting DROP and still create conntrack entries.

owen: also seeing iptables-nft chains created by np controller with lots of ephemeral rules. iptables counters show many hits on the namespace egress chain.

maria: snippets:```
# kubectl -n gpu-ns get networkpolicy deny-all -o yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-from-sidecars
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: inference}}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress: []
```
this denies all egress for inference pods unless other policies allow.

jin: if probes / heartbeats rely on UDP to other pods (kubelet/metrics/health checks) that aren't covered by allow rules, we get drops and conntrack churn from retries. UDP conntracks can be sticky.

sam: propose two immediate mitigations: 1) roll back the policy 2) increase conntrack table + tune garbage collection. which do we prefer for 10–20m hotfix?

maria: leaning rollback of the policy to restore connectivity quickly. can someone do a canary revert only for gpu-ns?

owen: I can patch the policy to add a temporary egress allow to cluster-internal CIDR and kube-system svc selectors. quick patch:```
patch: |
  spec:
    egress:
    - to:
      - ipBlock:
          cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
      - namespaceSelector:
          matchLabels:
            kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
```
this should let heartbeat traffic through while we debug.

ravi: small caveat: older conntrack entries won't free immediately; increase nf_conntrack_max to 524288 and lower timeout for UDP to 30s to help. sysctl change: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` and `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout=30`.

sre-bot: creating incident INC-2026-03018 to track. Priority P1 since multiple inference replicas impacted.

maria: applying the temporary egress allow now. will monitor.

deploy-bot: applied: networkpolicy/gpu-ns/deny-egress-from-sidecars patch by owen at 1779005600

owen: traffic restored within ~90s, heartbeats stable, NotReady cleared on 3 nodes. conntrack stats show insert_failed dropping to 0 after cleanup.

jin: next steps: 1) audit all networkpolicies that deny egress for namespaces with high-churn pods (sidecars / autoscaling inference pods) 2) add unit tests in policy CI simulating UDP heartbeats 3) tune cluster conntrack GC and monitor counters in the console.

sam: also let's add an annotation on gpu-ns to opt-out of strict egress deny until we have a vetted allowlist.

maria: filing follow-up ticket: DOCS-1423 (policy patterns for high-churn namespaces + conntrack sizing). thanks all. :white_check_mark:

ravi: will open a k8s change to make conntrack limits configurable in the node bootstrap so dedicated GPU pools get higher defaults.

maria: closing thread once the incident is resolved, will paste postmortem summary in #postmortems.
